name: SemiFab Constitution
description: An open constitution for semiconductor manufacturing operations monitoring and supply-chain control-tower software, expressed as ordinary and absolute provisions in the sense of Chapter 5, Definition 1 of the Digital Judiciary programme.

authorities.disjointness: A1: the three classes are pairwise disjoint over the deployment lifetime.

standing_declaration.note: A9 first limb. This corpus declares that a party holds contest standing adverse to grants, namely the trade compliance officer, so that the N-standing cases can exercise both postures. A deployment must replace this with its own fact.

provisions.title: No controlled technical data is released to a foreign person without a licence or a cited exception, and the check binds at role grant rather than at read
Controlled technical data never appears in logs, telemetry, support bundles or model context
Export records are append-only: the initial image is preserved and every change records who made it and when
A screening hit is never auto-cleared; screening-service failure is treated as a hit, never as a pass
provisions.source_status: US CFR public domain; CSL is US public domain

provisions.title: No change introduces a path that circumvents an export control, whatever its stated purpose

Every controlled artifact carries a recorded ECCN classification
A licence exception is cited by paragraph, never asserted in the abstract
The foreign direct product determination is recorded for covered items
End-use and end-user knowledge checks are documented for covered end uses
Geofencing is enforced at the authorisation layer, not in the client
Entity List footnote chains are evaluated, not just the direct party
Export records are retained for five years and are not disposed of while an agency request stands

provisions.family_title: ITAR technical data and defence articles
provisions.title: ITAR technical data is never released to a foreign person and lives only inside the segregated defence enclave; there is no de minimis threshold, no group-A carve-out and no risk acceptance
provisions.citation: 22 CFR 120.33 (technical data); 22 CFR 120.50(a)(2), 120.56 (release); 22 CFR 120.62 (foreign person); 22 CFR 127.1(a)
provisions.source_status: US CFR — public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); section numbers follow the 2022 ITAR reorganisation (87 FR 16396) and were checked against eCFR as of 6 Sept 2026. Absolute because unlicensed release is a strict-liability violation under 22 U.S.C. 2778 and 22 CFR 127.10 that no officer below the legislature may accept.

provisions.family_title: ITAR technical data and defence articles
provisions.title: Access to or transfer of a defence article or ITAR technical data proceeds only while DDTC registration is current and a licence or a section-cited exemption is bound into the grant
provisions.citation: 22 CFR 122.1 (registration); 22 CFR 123.1 (licence requirement); 22 CFR 125.4 (exemptions for technical data); 22 CFR 120.67 (empowered official)
provisions.source_status: US CFR — public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); registration and licensing sections checked against eCFR as of 6 Sept 2026.

provisions.family_title: ITAR technical data and defence articles
provisions.title: ITAR technical data is never stored or transmitted outside the authorised boundary unless every condition of the encryption carve-out holds: end-to-end encryption with a validated module, no storage in a proscribed country or Russia, and no decryption means held by a third party
provisions.citation: 22 CFR 120.54(a)(5) (activities that are not exports); 22 CFR 126.1 (proscribed destinations)
provisions.source_status: US CFR — public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); 120.54(a)(5) added by 84 FR 70887 (effective 25 March 2020) and retained through the 2022 reorganisation; checked as of 6 Sept 2026. Absolute because outside the carve-out the storage is itself an export under 120.50 and the same strict-liability floor as SF-IT-001 applies.

provisions.family_title: ITAR technical data and defence articles
provisions.title: A jurisdiction determination — USML category or CCL classification — is recorded for every defence-adjacent artifact before ingest, and an unresolved item is treated as ITAR until a determination says otherwise
provisions.citation: 22 CFR 120.4 (commodity jurisdiction); 22 CFR 121.1 (USML, Categories XI and XV); 15 CFR 774 Supplement 4 (order of review)
provisions.source_status: US CFR — public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); the fail-toward-ITAR default is corpus drafting, not a regulatory text, and is stated as such.

provisions.title: Counterparty screening against the SDN and consolidated sanctions lists, with fifty-percent ownership aggregation, is never bypassed for any counterparty class, and blocked-property handling is not configurable
provisions.citation: 31 CFR Part 501 (Reporting, Procedures and Penalties Regulations), 31 CFR 501.603, 501.604; OFAC Revised Guidance on Entities Owned by Blocked Persons (13 Aug 2014); 50 U.S.C. 1705
provisions.source_status: US CFR — public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); OFAC guidance is a US Treasury work, public domain, no explicit terms page located (research/03 §2.4). Absolute because IEEPA civil liability is strict and dealing in blocked property is prohibited regardless of intent; no officer may accept that risk.

provisions.title: A request to take a boycott-related action is never acted on and never dropped from the quarterly report, whether it arrives in a purchase order, a letter of credit or a portal form
provisions.source_status: US CFR — public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); Part 760 checked against eCFR as of 6 Sept 2026. Absolute because the reporting duty is statutory and quarterly; a dropped request is a failure to report that no risk owner may waive.
provisions.risk_framework: 5. Export Control Compliance (EAR/ITAR); Sanctions and Anti-Boycott

provisions.source_status: US CFR — public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); Part 850 effective 2 Jan 2025 and checked as of 6 Sept 2026. Directionally supported, not verified: the COINS Act (FY2026 NDAA, Dec 2025) expands the outbound regime and Treasury's implementing amendments to Part 850 were not confirmed as final.

provisions.title: Hazardous-gas monitoring alarms are never suppressed, filtered, rate-limited or re-thresholded by software, and reach the life-safety panel before any analytics path
provisions.citation: 29 U.S.C. 654(a)(1); 29 CFR 1910.119(d), (j), (l) where a covered process exists; 29 CFR 1910.1000; SEMI S2 (identifier only)
provisions.source_status: USC and CFR public domain; SEMI text not reproduced. Absolute because it is a life-safety floor: an employer duty under §654(a)(1) cannot be accepted as risk by a COO, and PSM management-of-change (1910.119(l)) forbids a software change to alarm behaviour outside the documented process.

provisions.title: Lockout/tagout, emergency-off and interlock states are read-only to software: no host command, status transformation or configuration can override, mask or reset them
provisions.source_status: US CFR public domain; SEMI text not reproduced. Absolute because the energy-control floor exists to protect the person at the tool; a software override is not a risk any owner may accept. Overlaps SF-SG-001 deliberately: that provision governs the signal path, this one the state semantics.

provisions.title: Effluent, emissions and chemical-reporting pipelines never drop, round or alter a monitoring result between measurement and the reported value, and a reporting job is never disabled by configuration
provisions.citation: 40 CFR 469 Subpart A; 40 CFR 122.41(j)(1), (j)(4), (l)(4); 33 U.S.C. 1319(c)(4); 42 U.S.C. 7413(c)(2); 40 CFR 63 Subpart BBBBB; 40 CFR 98 Subpart I; 40 CFR Part 705 (TSCA §8(a)(7) PFAS reporting)
provisions.source_status: US CFR and USC public domain. Absolute because knowingly false or omitted monitoring records are criminal under CWA §309(c)(4) and CAA §113(c)(2); integrity of the reported value is not risk-acceptable. Directionally supported, not verified: the Part 705 PFAS submission window was moved by EPA's May 2025 interim final rule and a Nov 2025 proposed rule; confirm 40 CFR 705.20 dates before relying on the PFAS clause.
